1	Equipment is frequently attached to the outside of a pipe after the pipe has been installed. Sensors, small tools, brackets, and lengths of conduit all have to be carried on a pipe that cannot be taken out of service, cannot be lifted, and has no free end over which a closed ring could be threaded. A clamp intended for that duty therefore has to open from the side, close around the pipe, and grip it firmly enough that the carried equipment keeps its position, while remaining removable so that the same clamp can be taken off and used again elsewhere.
2	
3	A clamp that opens from the side is split into parts, and the split is what makes the gripping problem difficult. Once the clamp body is divided, any drive element that runs around the body is divided with it. Gripping arrangements that answer this by driving the gripping surfaces of each part separately give up the fixed relationship between the two parts of the drive: the two sides of the clamp advance by amounts that depend on how each side is operated, so the clamp tends to settle off center on the pipe, and the load is shared unevenly between the gripping surfaces. Arrangements that instead pull the split body closed on the pipe, in the manner of a band or a two-bolt saddle, transfer the closing force through the joint at the split and rely on the pipe itself to react the closing motion, so the grip depends on how nearly the bore of the clamp matches the outside diameter of the pipe. Such an arrangement is commonly supplied with liners or inserts machined for one nominal pipe size, and a different pipe size calls for a different insert or a different clamp.
4	
5	Reusable clamping also has to deal with the force the operator applies. A hand lever gives the operator no measure of what has been done to the pipe. When the gripping elements have reached the pipe, further travel of the lever has to go somewhere, and in a rigid drive train it goes into whichever gripping element happens to touch first, so that one gripping surface is loaded far more than the others. Thin walled tube, coated pipe, and lined pipe are all damaged by that kind of concentrated loading, and the operator has no indication that it has occurred. Torque tools and gauges can be added to the installation, but they add a separate instrument to the task and, when they respond to the position of the gripping elements, they report the size of the pipe rather than the force in the grip.
6	
7	What has been lacking is a split clamp in which the drive that advances the gripping elements is itself restored to a single, continuous element by the act of closing the clamp, in which every gripping element is advanced from that one drive so that the clamp finds the center of the pipe by itself over a range of pipe sizes, and in which the travel remaining in the operator's lever after the gripping elements have landed on the pipe is absorbed within the clamp and reported to the operator as a loading condition rather than as a dimension.
8

1	The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition and with which the axis of a clamped pipe substantially coincides, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.
2	
3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the clamp 100 to be passed sideways onto a pipe 90 that is already installed, so that the clamp 100 need not be threaded over a free end of the pipe 90. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the clamp 100.
6	
7	Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and presents a concave pad face at its inner end, the pad being described below in connection with FIG. 3. The three jaw carriages 30 are the only members of the clamp 100 that touch the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped, and the position of the frame on the pipe 90 is established by them rather than by contact between the pipe 90 and a bore of the frame. The clamp 100 accordingly does not require a frame bore, liner, or insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
8	
9	The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide described below. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, a bracket, a length of conduit, or other equipment that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced, and the mounting boss 70 may be placed on either frame half at whatever circumferential position suits the equipment to be carried. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
10	
11	The segmented cam ring
12	
13	FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.
14	
15	The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are circumferentially facing drive faces, each pair being shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14 and the latch 16 is engaged, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end.
16	
17	Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. A clamp that must open from the side cannot carry a continuous drive ring across the split, and a divided drive must otherwise be operated separately in each half, with the result that the two halves advance their jaws by amounts that are not fixed relative to one another. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken automatically with each use and requires no separate assembly step.
18	
19	The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 passes through the segmented cam ring 20 and is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that circumferential movement of the ring produces a radial displacement of anything constrained to follow the slot. The three oblique slots 34 have the same inclination, so that a given rotation of the coupled ring advances each jaw carriage 30 by the same radial increment. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30, and is selected so that the available stroke of the coupled ring produces the radial travel required to span the intended range of pipe diameters, and so that the mechanical advantage at the jaw pads 40 is sufficient for the clamping force to be developed by hand at the latch 16. A shallower inclination gives greater mechanical advantage and less radial travel for a given stroke, and a steeper inclination gives more radial travel and less mechanical advantage.
20	
21	The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 faces circumferentially and is presented at a position on the ring where the latch can reach it, in the illustrated embodiment on the segment adjacent the latch end.
22	
23	The jaw carriages
24	
25	FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form an annular guide 18 that receives the segmented cam ring 20 and retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially. The annular guide 18 is formed in both frame halves, one arcuate portion of the annular guide 18 in each frame half, and the two arcuate portions register with one another in the closed condition to form a continuous annular path in which the coupled ring turns.
26	
27	The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective radial guide 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 may be a pin, a post, a roller, or a like projection able to bear against the sides of the oblique slot 34.
28	
29	The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. 46

52	
53	Variations
54	
55	The frame halves, the segmented cam ring 20, the jaw carriages 30, and the latch 16 may be made of any materials having the strength and stiffness required for the loads to be carried, and the parts that slide on one another, in particular the segmented cam ring 20 in the annular guide 18 and each jaw carriage 30 in its radial guide 38, may be surfaced or lubricated to reduce friction in the drive path. FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. The three jaw carriages 30 are the only members of the clamp 100 that touch the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped, and the position of the frame on the pipe 90 is established by them rather than by contact between the pipe 90 and a bore of the frame. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, a bracket, a length of conduit, or other equipment that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. content.text: I've read all inputs, the ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all four figure briefs. Here is the complete ledger review.

input.summary: Reviewed disclosure.md, conversation.md (which restates the disclosure verbatim and adds no further USER matter), brief.md, draft sections 01–10, numerals.md, and figures/fig-01.md through fig-04.md. The core architecture of the draft traces cleanly to the inventor's words: split semicircular frame halves with hinge and releasable latch, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave pads, a two-segment cam ring in an annular guide with complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends that couple on closing, followers in oblique slots producing synchronized inward travel, a latch-driven wedge acting on a ring drive face through a limited stroke, carriage return springs, the two latch positions, the force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing over a predetermined compression range, the non-participating mounting boss, and the install/remove sequence. Formalities check out: title matches the brief, no priority claim, no government support, abstract is under 150 words, no drafting notes or placeholders remain, all 25 numerals are unique and each appears in at least one figure brief. The problems are (a) a set of specific structures, materials, counts, variants, and results in the description and figure briefs that have no affirmative passage anywhere in the disclosure or conversation, and (b) three verifiable geometric contradictions among FIG. 2, FIG. 3, FIG. 4, and the description text concerning slot orientation, ring retention, and the wedge/drive-face interface. Fifteen findings follow, each with the candidate wording, the nearest source passage, and a filing-clean fix.

findings.title: Exclusive assertion that the jaw carriages are the only parts touching the pipe is untraced
findings.detail: The description asserts an exclusivity relationship (nothing but the carriages contacts the pipe) and a negative structural fact (no frame bore contact), and the Summary repeats it. The disclosure never says the jaw pads are the sole contact members or that the frame bore stands clear of the pipe; it says only that each carriage carries a pad that bears on the pipe without requiring a tool-specific diameter. No affirmative USER passage supports the exclusivity or the bore/no-bore relationship. The sentence also mis-attributes contact to the carriages when the description and claim 1 put the contact on the pivoting jaw pad 40 carried by the carriage.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The three jaw carriages 30 are the only members of the clamp 100 that touch the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped, and the position of the frame on the pipe 90 is established by them rather than by contact between the pipe 90 and a bore of the frame." Summary: "The frame therefore takes up its position on the pipe from the jaws rather than from a bore matched to a nominal pipe size". Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter." There is no affirmative passage about sole contact or about a frame bore.
findings.fix: In ¶7 replace the quoted sentence with: "The jaw pads carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped." In draft/06-summary.md ¶5 replace "The frame therefore takes up its position on the pipe from the jaws rather than from a bore matched to a nominal pipe size, and the pivoting concave jaw pads seat on the pipe without an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter." with "The pivoting concave jaw pads seat on the pipe without an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter."

findings.title: Jaw pad facing/lining material and softer-than-pipe material are untraced
findings.detail: The description adds a material variant for the bearing face, including a comparative hardness relationship and named pipe conditions (coated, thin walled). The disclosure says nothing about pad materials, facings, or liners. Coated and thin-walled pipe appear only in the Background as prior-art context, which cannot support invention text.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The bearing face may be faced or lined with a material chosen for the pipe to be gripped, for example a material softer than the pipe surface where a coated or thin walled pipe is to be clamped." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe" — no affirmative passage on pad material, facing, or lining exists in the disclosure or conversation.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence from ¶31 in its entirety. No replacement text is needed; the preceding sentences already state the disclosed function of the concave pivoting face.

findings.title: Follower embodied as pin, post, roller, or like projection is untraced
findings.detail: The description offers four alternative embodiments of the follower. A roller in particular changes the mechanics of the slot interface (rolling rather than sliding contact). The disclosure identifies the part only as "a follower" received in the oblique slot and gives it no form.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The follower 32 may be a pin, a post, a roller, or a like projection able to bear against the sides of the oblique slot 34." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring." No affirmative passage names any follower form.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34." (FIG. 3 may keep its generic post outline, which is a permitted depiction convention, so long as the text asserts no form.)

findings.title: FIG. 2 depicts an overlapping stepped lap joint at both cam-ring joints; the joint topology is untraced
findings.detail: The brief specifies a particular joint topology: each segment end is stepped so that the outer part of one segment and the inner part of the other reach past the joint in opposite senses, meeting along two circumferentially facing surfaces. An interdigitated lap joint conveys technical substance (radial interlock at the joint, force transfer in both circumferential senses through overlapping tongues) that the disclosure never provides. Calling it "drawn schematically" does not convert it into a permitted convention, because it adds a structural relationship rather than merely choosing an outline. A plain abutting pair of circumferentially facing end surfaces is the shape-neutral choice and is fully consistent with the description's characterization of the faces.
findings.evidence: Candidate (fig-02.md): "the outer part of the end of the first cam ring segment 22 reaches past the joint and the inner part of the end of the second cam ring segment 24 reaches past it in the opposite sense, the steps meeting along two short circumferentially facing surfaces." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring." No affirmative passage describes overlapping, stepped, or interlocking segment ends.
findings.fix: In fig-02.md replace both joint paragraphs with: "At the left joint the two segment ends meet along plain complementary surfaces that face circumferentially, one on the end of the first cam ring segment 22 and one on the end of the second cam ring segment 24. Those surfaces are the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26." and the corresponding sentence for the right joint and numeral 28. Make no change to the description or claims, which are already shape-neutral.

findings.title: FIG. 4 specifies a count of four dished (Belleville) washers for the force-limiting spring stack
findings.detail: The brief fixes both the element count (four) and the element type (dished washers / disc springs in a chevron section) for the force-limiting spring stack. Counts and element form are technical substance, not depiction convention. The disclosure names only "a force-limiting spring stack", and the description deliberately keeps it generic ("one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack"), so the figure is more specific than both the source and the text it illustrates.
findings.evidence: Candidate (fig-04.md): "a short column of four stacked dished washers is drawn schematically, each washer a shallow open chevron lying on its side". Nearest source (disclosure ¶3): "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge". No affirmative passage states the number or type of resilient elements. Draft text (¶41): "The force-limiting spring stack 54 comprises one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack".
findings.fix: In fig-04.md replace the sentence with: "To the right of that block, a compression spring is drawn schematically as a zigzag line running from the upright right face of the wedge 52 to a flat plate at the right end. That spring is the force-limiting spring stack 54." This matches the neutral spring convention already used for the carriage return spring 44 in FIG. 3 and removes both the count and the washer form.

findings.title: Ring drive face depicted on a discrete radially projecting lug
findings.detail: Both figure briefs place the ring drive face 36 on a short rectangular lug projecting radially outward from the second cam ring segment close to the latch-end joint. A discrete projection outside the annulus at a stated circumferential location conveys structure and relative location (it must clear the annular guide, and it fixes where the wedge reaches the ring). The disclosure says only that the wedge is driven "against a drive face of the cam ring" and gives the face no carrier, form, or position.
findings.evidence: Candidate (fig-02.md): "A short rectangular lug projects radially outward from the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment 24, close to the right joint. Its circumferentially facing end surface, the surface facing away from the right joint, is the ring drive face 36." Candidate (fig-04.md): "A short rectangular lug projects upward from the band near its right end, and the flat end surface of that lug, facing right, is the ring drive face 36." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke."
findings.fix: In fig-02.md replace the lug paragraph with: "A short circumferentially facing surface is formed on the second cam ring segment 24 near the right joint. That surface is the ring drive face 36." In fig-04.md replace the lug sentence with: "The right end of the band terminates in a flat surface facing right; that surface is the ring drive face 36," and update the numeral targets in both briefs to point at that surface. Leave the description unchanged; it already says only that the face "faces circumferentially and is presented at a position on the ring where the latch can reach it."

findings.title: Carriage return spring seating (abutment and shoulder) asserted in the description is untraced
findings.detail: The description asserts a specific spring type and two specific reaction surfaces. The disclosure states only that a spring biases each carriage outward and says nothing about the spring's type or where it seats. FIG. 3 must show the spring somewhere, and its ledge/flange arrangement is an acceptable depiction convention, but the application text may not convert that renderer's choice into an asserted structure and connection.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "In the illustrated embodiment the carriage return spring 44 is a compression spring seated between an abutment of the radial guide 38 and a shoulder of the jaw carriage 30." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released."
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The carriage return spring 44 acts between the jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge the jaw carriage 30 radially outward." In ¶55 correspondingly replace "may act between the jaw carriage 30 and its radial guide 38 as illustrated, or elsewhere on the jaw carriage 30, provided that" with "may act at any location on the jaw carriage 30, provided that".

findings.title: Mounting boss placement freedom and "a bracket" in the supported-equipment list are untraced
findings.detail: Two additions. First, the description enlarges the disclosed list of carried equipment with "a bracket" and "other equipment"; the disclosure lists only a sensor, tool, or conduit (and the claims correctly recite only those three, so the description is broader than both the source and the claims). Second, the description asserts that the boss may be placed on either frame half at any circumferential position — a positional variant the disclosure never grants; it says only that the frame may carry the boss outside the annular guide.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, a bracket, a length of conduit, or other equipment that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100." and "the mounting boss 70 may be placed on either frame half at whatever circumferential position suits the equipment to be carried." Nearest source (disclosure ¶4): "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization." ("Brackets" appear only in Background ¶1 as prior-art context.)
findings.fix: In ¶9 change the first quoted sentence to: "The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100." Delete the clause ", and the mounting boss 70 may be placed on either frame half at whatever circumferential position suits the equipment to be carried", ending that sentence after "the jaws are advanced."

findings.title: Self-centering result claimed and stated as an express limitation without an affirmative source passage
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 8; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶29 last sentence; draft/05-background.md ¶7
findings.detail: Claim 8 recites the centering of the frame on the pipe as an express result limitation, and the description and Background bridge paragraph repeat it. The disclosure never states that the clamp centers itself, finds the pipe center, or is self-centering; it states synchronized inward travel of the three carriages and independence from a tool-specific pipe diameter. Centering may well follow geometrically from equal synchronized advance of three distributed jaws, but there is no affirmative inventor passage stating the result, and the working title in brief.md ("Self-Centering...") is authority for the title only, never for technical invention matter. The title itself may stand as filed.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 8): "...such that rotation of the coupled ring through a given angle advances the three jaw carriages by equal radial increments and the frame takes up a position centered on a pipe received in the frame." Candidate (¶29): "The jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together and the frame takes up a position centered on the pipe." Candidate (Background ¶7): "so that the clamp finds the center of the pipe by itself over a range of pipe sizes". Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages." No passage states centering.
findings.fix: In claim 8 delete "and the frame takes up a position centered on a pipe received in the frame", ending the claim at "equal radial increments." In ¶29 delete "and the frame takes up a position centered on the pipe", ending at "close on the pipe together." In Background ¶7 replace "so that the clamp finds the center of the pipe by itself over a range of pipe sizes" with "so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes". Retain the title as given in the brief.

findings.title: FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 depict the oblique slot in mutually incompatible orientations
findings.detail: FIG. 2 shows each oblique slot as an opening passing through the flat annulus (i.e. an axial through-slot) that lies wholly within the radial width of the annulus, breaking neither the inner nor the outer boundary. FIG. 3 is sectioned in a plane containing the radial direction and the frame axis with radially outward toward the top, and shows the slot as an opening passing through the ring "from top to bottom", i.e. from the radially inner face to the radially outer face, dividing the ring section into left and right portions and receiving a post that rises radially from the jaw carriage. An axial through-slot cannot be entered by a radially rising post, and in the FIG. 3 section plane an axial slot would appear as a void running left-to-right at one radial level rather than as a top-to-bottom opening. The two briefs cannot both be rendered. The disclosure fixes neither orientation ("a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring"), so either may be chosen, but one must be chosen consistently.
findings.evidence: fig-02.md: "Three elongated openings pass through the annulus... lying within the width of the annulus and clearly inclined to the radius at its own position". fig-03.md: "It is interrupted at its middle by a rectangular opening passing through it from top to bottom, dividing its outline into a left portion and a right portion. That opening is the oblique slot 34." and "A short post rises from its upper end into the opening in the segmented cam ring 20".
findings.fix: Adopt the FIG. 2 orientation (axial through-slot) and conform FIG. 3. In fig-03.md ¶3 replace the last two sentences with: "It is interrupted at its middle by a rectangular opening passing through it from left to right, so that a radially outer portion and a radially inner portion of its outline remain above and below the opening. That opening is the oblique slot 34." In fig-03.md ¶5 replace "A short post rises from its upper end into the opening in the segmented cam ring 20, its sides facing the sides of that opening." with "A short post extends from its upper end into the opening in the segmented cam ring 20, its sides facing the radially outer and radially inner sides of that opening." Adjust the numeral 32 and 34 targets accordingly.

findings.title: FIG. 3 shows the annular guide open radially outward with clearance at each side, contradicting the stated retention of the cam ring
findings.detail: The description and claim 10 require the annular guide to retain the cam ring against radial (and, in the description, axial) displacement while permitting circumferential movement. FIG. 3 shows the guide as a recess "open toward the top", and in that view radially outward is toward the top, so nothing retains the ring radially outward; it further shows the ring "narrower than the recess so that a clear space remains at each side of it", so nothing retains it axially either. As drawn, the ring would simply lift out of the frame.
findings.evidence: fig-03.md View: "Radially outward is toward the top." fig-03.md ¶3: "The upper opening is a rectangular recess, wider than deep, open toward the top. That recess is the annular guide 18. Received in it is a hatched rectangular block, narrower than the recess so that a clear space remains at each side of it." Description ¶25: "an annular guide 18 that receives the segmented cam ring 20 and retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially." Claim 10: "each arcuate portion retaining the respective cam ring segment against radial displacement while permitting circumferential movement".
findings.fix: In fig-03.md ¶3 replace the first two sentences with: "The upper opening is a rectangular groove, wider than deep, formed in the body and closed on its radially outer side, the groove opening toward the left of the view through a mouth narrower than the groove so that a lip overhangs the groove on the radially outer side. That groove is the annular guide 18." and replace "narrower than the recess so that a clear space remains at each side of it" with "filling the groove in the radial direction and retained in it by the lip, a small running clearance remaining at each side". Update the numeral 18 target to "the wall of the groove above the block".

findings.title: FIG. 4 wedge/drive-face interface is self-contradictory and inconsistent with the described wedging action
findings.detail: Two contradictions. (1) Within fig-04.md, the ring drive face is a flat surface facing right, while the wedge's left face is inclined, yet the brief says the inclined face "bears flat against" that surface; an inclined plane and an upright plane cannot bear flat on one another. (2) The description states that the wedge's inclined face converts the wedge's advance into circumferential movement of the ring, which requires the wedge advance direction and the ring's circumferential direction to differ. FIG. 4 shows the wedge advancing leftward directly along the direction in which the drive face is pushed, so no conversion occurs and the inclined face has no function.
findings.evidence: fig-04.md ¶2: "the flat end surface of that lug, facing right, is the ring drive face 36." fig-04.md ¶4: "a block whose left face is inclined and bears flat against the end surface of the lug, and whose right face is upright. That block is the wedge 52." Description ¶39: "The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20".
findings.fix: Conform FIG. 4 to the described wedging action. In fig-04.md ¶4 replace the paragraph with: "At the left of the cavity is a block that is guided to move downward in the view, toward the band. Its lower left face is inclined and bears against the ring drive face 36, which is correspondingly inclined, so that downward movement of the block drives the band to the left. That block is the wedge 52." In fig-04.md ¶2 replace "the flat end surface of that lug, facing right, is the ring drive face 36" with "the surface at the right end of the band, inclined so as to face upward and to the right, is the ring drive face 36". Move the latch handle link so that it drives the wedge downward, and update the numeral 36 and 52 targets accordingly.

findings.title: Untraced latch function statements: repositioning along the pipe and absence of a separate securing element
findings.detail: Two functional assertions have no affirmative source. The disclosure says the first latch position "holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping"; it does not say the clamp can be slid or turned along the pipe in that position. The disclosure says the second position is over-center; it does not state that the clamp therefore needs no separate securing element, which is a negative structural assertion about what the clamp omits.
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶39): "the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44 and the clamp 100 can still be slid or turned along the pipe 90 to its intended position" and "so that the latch 16 stays closed without a separate securing element". Candidate (¶49): "in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping and can still be positioned along the pipe 90". Nearest source (disclosure ¶3): "The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe."
findings.fix: In ¶39 delete " and the clamp 100 can still be slid or turned along the pipe 90 to its intended position" and delete ", so that the latch 16 stays closed without a separate securing element". In ¶49 delete " and can still be positioned along the pipe 90" and delete "When the clamp 100 is where it is wanted, " so the sentence begins "The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position."

findings.title: Untraced design-parameter teaching and untraced variants in the Variations paragraph
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶19, last sentence; ¶55, first and fourth sentences
findings.detail: Three items rest on general engineering knowledge rather than inventor support: the mechanical-advantage/travel trade-off as a function of slot inclination; surface treatment or lubrication of the sliding interfaces; and an alternative in which the wedge acts on the ring drive face through an intermediate sliding member. The disclosure describes none of these. Common engineering knowledge is not inventor support, and the intermediate-member alternative in particular adds a drive-train element.
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶19): "A shallower inclination gives greater mechanical advantage and less radial travel for a given stroke, and a steeper inclination gives more radial travel and less mechanical advantage." Candidate (¶55): "may be surfaced or lubricated to reduce friction in the drive path" and "The wedge 52 may act on the ring drive face 36 directly or through an intermediate sliding member, provided that the force-limiting spring stack 54 remains in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." No passage addresses inclination trade-offs, surface treatment, lubrication, or an intermediate member.
findings.fix: Delete the last sentence of ¶19. In ¶55 delete ", and the parts that slide on one another, in particular the segmented cam ring 20 in the annular guide 18 and each jaw carriage 30 in its radial guide 38, may be surfaced or lubricated to reduce friction in the drive path", ending that sentence after "the loads to be carried". Delete the sentence beginning "The wedge 52 may act on the ring drive face 36 directly or through an intermediate sliding member" and, to preserve the disclosed relationship, replace it with: "The force-limiting spring stack 54 lies in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52."

findings.title: FIG. 1 shows the jaw pad merged into the jaw carriage, and claim antecedents for the return springs and jaw carriages are inconsistent
findings.where: figures/fig-01.md ¶6; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶7; draft/09-claims.md claim 1 last element, claim 7, claim 17
findings.detail: Three small consistency defects. (1) FIG. 1 draws each jaw carriage as one block "ending in a shallow concave pad face", with no separate pivoted jaw pad 40, whereas claim 1 and ¶31 require a jaw pad pivotally mounted on the carriage; ¶7's phrasing ("presents a concave pad face at its inner end") papers over the omission rather than resolving it. (2) Claim 1 introduces "a carriage return spring" in the singular and then refers to "the carriage return springs" in the plural in the same element; claim 7 likewise recites "the carriage return springs". (3) Claim 17 introduces "jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp" without a number and then recites "advancing three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp", so the count is introduced twice.
findings.evidence: fig-01.md: "Each is drawn as a block that crosses the inner boundary of the ring and reaches radially inward, ending in a shallow concave pad face that meets the outer surface of the pipe 90." Claim 1: "a carriage return spring biasing each jaw carriage outwardly, such that release of the latch permits the carriage return springs to retract the jaw carriages." Claim 17: "...with jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp retracted;" then "advancing three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp inwardly in synchronism".
findings.fix: (1) In fig-01.md ¶6 replace the quoted sentence with: "Each is drawn as a block that crosses the inner boundary of the ring and reaches radially inward, and carries at its inner end a separate member joined to it at a small circle shown as a pivot, that member having a shallow concave face that meets the outer surface of the pipe 90. That member is the jaw pad 40." Add to the FIG. 1 numeral list: "40 jaw pad: target well inside the member at the inner end of the topmost jaw carriage." (2) In claim 1 recite: "three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages outwardly, such that release of the latch permits the carriage return springs to retract the jaw carriages." (3) In claim 17 change "with jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp retracted" to "with three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp retracted" and change "advancing three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp" to "advancing the three jaw carriages".

findings.detail: The brief fixes both the element count (four) and the element type (dished washers / disc springs in a chevron section) for the force-limiting spring stack. Counts and element form are technical substance, not depiction convention. The disclosure names only "a force-limiting spring stack", and the description deliberately keeps it generic ("one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack"), so the figure is more specific than both the source and the text it illustrates.
findings.evidence: Candidate (fig-04.md): "a short column of four stacked dished washers is drawn schematically, each washer a shallow open chevron lying on its side". Nearest source (disclosure ¶3): "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge". No affirmative passage states the number or type of resilient elements. Draft text (¶41): "The force-limiting spring stack 54 comprises one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack".
findings.fix: In fig-04.md replace the sentence with: "To the right of that block, a compression spring is drawn schematically as a zigzag line running from the upright right face of the wedge 52 to a flat plate at the right end. That spring is the force-limiting spring stack 54." This matches the neutral spring convention already used for the carriage return spring 44 in FIG. 3 and removes both the count and the washer form.

findings.title: Ring drive face depicted on a discrete radially projecting lug
findings.detail: Both figure briefs place the ring drive face 36 on a short rectangular lug projecting radially outward from the second cam ring segment close to the latch-end joint. A discrete projection outside the annulus at a stated circumferential location conveys structure and relative location (it must clear the annular guide, and it fixes where the wedge reaches the ring). The disclosure says only that the wedge is driven "against a drive face of the cam ring" and gives the face no carrier, form, or position.
findings.evidence: Candidate (fig-02.md): "A short rectangular lug projects radially outward from the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment 24, close to the right joint. Its circumferentially facing end surface, the surface facing away from the right joint, is the ring drive face 36." Candidate (fig-04.md): "A short rectangular lug projects upward from the band near its right end, and the flat end surface of that lug, facing right, is the ring drive face 36." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke."
findings.fix: In fig-02.md replace the lug paragraph with: "A short circumferentially facing surface is formed on the second cam ring segment 24 near the right joint. That surface is the ring drive face 36." In fig-04.md replace the lug sentence with: "The right end of the band terminates in a flat surface facing right; that surface is the ring drive face 36," and update the numeral targets in both briefs to point at that surface. Leave the description unchanged; it already says only that the face "faces circumferentially and is presented at a position on the ring where the latch can reach it."

findings.title: Carriage return spring seating (abutment and shoulder) asserted in the description is untraced
findings.detail: The description asserts a specific spring type and two specific reaction surfaces. The disclosure states only that a spring biases each carriage outward and says nothing about the spring's type or where it seats. FIG. 3 must show the spring somewhere, and its ledge/flange arrangement is an acceptable depiction convention, but the application text may not convert that renderer's choice into an asserted structure and connection.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "In the illustrated embodiment the carriage return spring 44 is a compression spring seated between an abutment of the radial guide 38 and a shoulder of the jaw carriage 30." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released."
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The carriage return spring 44 acts between the jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge the jaw carriage 30 radially outward." In ¶55 correspondingly replace "may act between the jaw carriage 30 and its radial guide 38 as illustrated, or elsewhere on the jaw carriage 30, provided that" with "may act at any location on the jaw carriage 30, provided that".

findings.title: Mounting boss placement freedom and "a bracket" in the supported-equipment list are untraced
findings.detail: Two additions. First, the description enlarges the disclosed list of carried equipment with "a bracket" and "other equipment"; the disclosure lists only a sensor, tool, or conduit (and the claims correctly recite only those three, so the description is broader than both the source and the claims). Second, the description asserts that the boss may be placed on either frame half at any circumferential position — a positional variant the disclosure never grants; it says only that the frame may carry the boss outside the annular guide.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, a bracket, a length of conduit, or other equipment that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100." and "the mounting boss 70 may be placed on either frame half at whatever circumferential position suits the equipment to be carried." Nearest source (disclosure ¶4): "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization." ("Brackets" appear only in Background ¶1 as prior-art context.)
findings.fix: In ¶9 change the first quoted sentence to: "The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100." Delete the clause ", and the mounting boss 70 may be placed on either frame half at whatever circumferential position suits the equipment to be carried", ending that sentence after "the jaws are advanced."

findings.title: Self-centering result claimed and stated as an express limitation without an affirmative source passage
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 8; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶29 last sentence; draft/05-background.md ¶7
findings.detail: Claim 8 recites the centering of the frame on the pipe as an express result limitation, and the description and Background bridge paragraph repeat it. The disclosure never states that the clamp centers itself, finds the pipe center, or is self-centering; it states synchronized inward travel of the three carriages and independence from a tool-specific pipe diameter. Centering may well follow geometrically from equal synchronized advance of three distributed jaws, but there is no affirmative inventor passage stating the result, and the working title in brief.md ("Self-Centering...") is authority for the title only, never for technical invention matter. The title itself may stand as filed.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 8): "...such that rotation of the coupled ring through a given angle advances the three jaw carriages by equal radial increments and the frame takes up a position centered on a pipe received in the frame." Candidate (¶29): "The jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together and the frame takes up a position centered on the pipe." Candidate (Background ¶7): "so that the clamp finds the center of the pipe by itself over a range of pipe sizes". Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages." No passage states centering.
findings.fix: In claim 8 delete "and the frame takes up a position centered on a pipe received in the frame", ending the claim at "equal radial increments." In ¶29 delete "and the frame takes up a position centered on the pipe", ending at "close on the pipe together." In Background ¶7 replace "so that the clamp finds the center of the pipe by itself over a range of pipe sizes" with "so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes". Retain the title as given in the brief.

findings.title: FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 depict the oblique slot in mutually incompatible orientations
findings.detail: FIG. 2 shows each oblique slot as an opening passing through the flat annulus (i.e. an axial through-slot) that lies wholly within the radial width of the annulus, breaking neither the inner nor the outer boundary. FIG. 3 is sectioned in a plane containing the radial direction and the frame axis with radially outward toward the top, and shows the slot as an opening passing through the ring "from top to bottom", i.e. from the radially inner face to the radially outer face, dividing the ring section into left and right portions and receiving a post that rises radially from the jaw carriage. An axial through-slot cannot be entered by a radially rising post, and in the FIG. 3 section plane an axial slot would appear as a void running left-to-right at one radial level rather than as a top-to-bottom opening. The two briefs cannot both be rendered. The disclosure fixes neither orientation ("a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring"), so either may be chosen, but one must be chosen consistently.
findings.evidence: fig-02.md: "Three elongated openings pass through the annulus... lying within the width of the annulus and clearly inclined to the radius at its own position". fig-03.md: "It is interrupted at its middle by a rectangular opening passing through it from top to bottom, dividing its outline into a left portion and a right portion. That opening is the oblique slot 34." and "A short post rises from its upper end into the opening in the segmented cam ring 20".
findings.fix: Adopt the FIG. 2 orientation (axial through-slot) and conform FIG. 3. In fig-03.md ¶3 replace the last two sentences with: "It is interrupted at its middle by a rectangular opening passing through it from left to right, so that a radially outer portion and a radially inner portion of its outline remain above and below the opening. That opening is the oblique slot 34." In fig-03.md ¶5 replace "A short post rises from its upper end into the opening in the segmented cam ring 20, its sides facing the sides of that opening." with "A short post extends from its upper end into the opening in the segmented cam ring 20, its sides facing the radially outer and radially inner sides of that opening." Adjust the numeral 32 and 34 targets accordingly.

findings.title: FIG. 3 shows the annular guide open radially outward with clearance at each side, contradicting the stated retention of the cam ring
findings.detail: The description and claim 10 require the annular guide to retain the cam ring against radial (and, in the description, axial) displacement while permitting circumferential movement. FIG. 3 shows the guide as a recess "open toward the top", and in that view radially outward is toward the top, so nothing retains the ring radially outward; it further shows the ring "narrower than the recess so that a clear space remains at each side of it", so nothing retains it axially either. As drawn, the ring would simply lift out of the frame.
findings.evidence: fig-03.md View: "Radially outward is toward the top." fig-03.md ¶3: "The upper opening is a rectangular recess, wider than deep, open toward the top. That recess is the annular guide 18. Received in it is a hatched rectangular block, narrower than the recess so that a clear space remains at each side of it." Description ¶25: "an annular guide 18 that receives the segmented cam ring 20 and retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially." Claim 10: "each arcuate portion retaining the respective cam ring segment against radial displacement while permitting circumferential movement".
findings.fix: In fig-03.md ¶3 replace the first two sentences with: "The upper opening is a rectangular groove, wider than deep, formed in the body and closed on its radially outer side, the groove opening toward the left of the view through a mouth narrower than the groove so that a lip overhangs the groove on the radially outer side. That groove is the annular guide 18." and replace "narrower than the recess so that a clear space remains at each side of it" with "filling the groove in the radial direction and retained in it by the lip, a small running clearance remaining at each side". Update the numeral 18 target to "the wall of the groove above the block".

findings.title: FIG. 4 wedge/drive-face interface is self-contradictory and inconsistent with the described wedging action
findings.detail: Two contradictions. (1) Within fig-04.md, the ring drive face is a flat surface facing right, while the wedge's left face is inclined, yet the brief says the inclined face "bears flat against" that surface; an inclined plane and an upright plane cannot bear flat on one another. (2) The description states that the wedge's inclined face converts the wedge's advance into circumferential movement of the ring, which requires the wedge advance direction and the ring's circumferential direction to differ. FIG. 4 shows the wedge advancing leftward directly along the direction in which the drive face is pushed, so no conversion occurs and the inclined face has no function.
findings.evidence: fig-04.md ¶2: "the flat end surface of that lug, facing right, is the ring drive face 36." fig-04.md ¶4: "a block whose left face is inclined and bears flat against the end surface of the lug, and whose right face is upright. That block is the wedge 52." Description ¶39: "The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20".
findings.fix: Conform FIG. 4 to the described wedging action. In fig-04.md ¶4 replace the paragraph with: "At the left of the cavity is a block that is guided to move downward in the view, toward the band. Its lower left face is inclined and bears against the ring drive face 36, which is correspondingly inclined, so that downward movement of the block drives the band to the left. That block is the wedge 52." In fig-04.md ¶2 replace "the flat end surface of that lug, facing right, is the ring drive face 36" with "the surface at the right end of the band, inclined so as to face upward and to the right, is the ring drive face 36". Move the latch handle link so that it drives the wedge downward, and update the numeral 36 and 52 targets accordingly.

findings.title: Untraced latch function statements: repositioning along the pipe and absence of a separate securing element
findings.detail: Two functional assertions have no affirmative source. The disclosure says the first latch position "holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping"; it does not say the clamp can be slid or turned along the pipe in that position. The disclosure says the second position is over-center; it does not state that the clamp therefore needs no separate securing element, which is a negative structural assertion about what the clamp omits.
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶39): "the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44 and the clamp 100 can still be slid or turned along the pipe 90 to its intended position" and "so that the latch 16 stays closed without a separate securing element". Candidate (¶49): "in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping and can still be positioned along the pipe 90". Nearest source (disclosure ¶3): "The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe."
findings.fix: In ¶39 delete " and the clamp 100 can still be slid or turned along the pipe 90 to its intended position" and delete ", so that the latch 16 stays closed without a separate securing element". In ¶49 delete " and can still be positioned along the pipe 90" and delete "When the clamp 100 is where it is wanted, " so the sentence begins "The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position."

findings.title: Untraced design-parameter teaching and untraced variants in the Variations paragraph
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶19, last sentence; ¶55, first and fourth sentences
findings.detail: Three items rest on general engineering knowledge rather than inventor support: the mechanical-advantage/travel trade-off as a function of slot inclination; surface treatment or lubrication of the sliding interfaces; and an alternative in which the wedge acts on the ring drive face through an intermediate sliding member. The disclosure describes none of these. Common engineering knowledge is not inventor support, and the intermediate-member alternative in particular adds a drive-train element.
findings.evidence: Candidate (¶19): "A shallower inclination gives greater mechanical advantage and less radial travel for a given stroke, and a steeper inclination gives more radial travel and less mechanical advantage." Candidate (¶55): "may be surfaced or lubricated to reduce friction in the drive path" and "The wedge 52 may act on the ring drive face 36 directly or through an intermediate sliding member, provided that the force-limiting spring stack 54 remains in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52." Nearest source (disclosure ¶2): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." No passage addresses inclination trade-offs, surface treatment, lubrication, or an intermediate member.
findings.fix: Delete the last sentence of ¶19. In ¶55 delete ", and the parts that slide on one another, in particular the segmented cam ring 20 in the annular guide 18 and each jaw carriage 30 in its radial guide 38, may be surfaced or lubricated to reduce friction in the drive path", ending that sentence after "the loads to be carried". Delete the sentence beginning "The wedge 52 may act on the ring drive face 36 directly or through an intermediate sliding member" and, to preserve the disclosed relationship, replace it with: "The force-limiting spring stack 54 lies in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52."

findings.title: FIG. 1 shows the jaw pad merged into the jaw carriage, and claim antecedents for the return springs and jaw carriages are inconsistent
findings.where: figures/fig-01.md ¶6; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶7; draft/09-claims.md claim 1 last element, claim 7, claim 17
findings.detail: Three small consistency defects. (1) FIG. 1 draws each jaw carriage as one block "ending in a shallow concave pad face", with no separate pivoted jaw pad 40, whereas claim 1 and ¶31 require a jaw pad pivotally mounted on the carriage; ¶7's phrasing ("presents a concave pad face at its inner end") papers over the omission rather than resolving it. (2) Claim 1 introduces "a carriage return spring" in the singular and then refers to "the carriage return springs" in the plural in the same element; claim 7 likewise recites "the carriage return springs". (3) Claim 17 introduces "jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp" without a number and then recites "advancing three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp", so the count is introduced twice.
findings.evidence: fig-01.md: "Each is drawn as a block that crosses the inner boundary of the ring and reaches radially inward, ending in a shallow concave pad face that meets the outer surface of the pipe 90." Claim 1: "a carriage return spring biasing each jaw carriage outwardly, such that release of the latch permits the carriage return springs to retract the jaw carriages." Claim 17: "...with jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp retracted;" then "advancing three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp inwardly in synchronism".
findings.fix: (1) In fig-01.md ¶6 replace the quoted sentence with: "Each is drawn as a block that crosses the inner boundary of the ring and reaches radially inward, and carries at its inner end a separate member joined to it at a small circle shown as a pivot, that member having a shallow concave face that meets the outer surface of the pipe 90. That member is the jaw pad 40." Add to the FIG. 1 numeral list: "40 jaw pad: target well inside the member at the inner end of the topmost jaw carriage." (2) In claim 1 recite: "three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages outwardly, such that release of the latch permits the carriage return springs to retract the jaw carriages." (3) In claim 17 change "with jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp retracted" to "with three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp retracted" and change "advancing three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp" to "advancing the three jaw carriages".
